I wish this review were about gameplay, graphics, or missions… but I haven’t been able to play any of that because I’ve been stuck dealing with Rockstar’s absurdly slow password reset system. I got locked out of my account, and what should’ve been a simple “click link, reset password, get back in” turned into a multi‑hour waiting game. For 8 Days, that’s just unacceptable.

The worst part is how outdated the whole process feels. You request a reset, and then you sit there refreshing your inbox like it’s 2005, hoping the email finally arrives. When it does, it’s often delayed so long that the link is practically useless by the time you get it. I’ve spent more time trying to regain access to the game than I’ve ever spent actually playing it on Steam.

For a studio with the resources Rockstar has, this is embarrassing. GTA 5 is supposed to be a premium experience, but the account system feels like it was built by a completely different company—one that doesn’t care about user experience at all. If you ever lose access to your account, prepare to wait, and wait, and wait some more.

citations.review_text: I've loved this game ever since I first played it on my Xbox 360. I've played it on PC, PS4, and lately on PS5. The single-player is still a 10/10 experience. Whoever says EA is a bad company clearly hasn't experienced a Rockstar game before. Ranging from customer support that doesn't give a modicum of a crap about the issues players experience (for example, I filled out a ticket for an issue I was having back in June, got a reply almost exactly a month later, and the agent who responded to it closed the ticket pretty much right after he messaged me, not even giving me a chance to respond), to not patching issues that have been in the game for literally years, to trying to bottleneck players into spending obscene amounts of money on microtransactions (with the alternative being tons of grinding, not helped by them nerfing the few moneymaking techniques that are actually FUN), and harshly punishing players for things that either aren't their fault - such as an ex-friend of mine being banned and having his character deleted as a consequence of something a hacker in his online lobby did - or are poorly designed/described by Rockstar themselves.

Given how much of a grind-heavy, poorly-managed experience GTA Online is (as well as how the story mode of GTA V is a considerable letdown compared to GTA IV and its DLC), I don't pity anyone who's foolish enough to buy or especially preorder GTA VI, let alone anyone who would play this one. The nicest things I can say about GTA V/Online are that the gameplay itself and graphics are pretty good, but the issues I mentioned before render this beyond salvaging.

Rockstar Games has become one of the most anti-consumer companies in the industry. The pricing of in-game items encourages players to buy Shark Cards or GTA+, making the grind so time-consuming that spending money becomes the practical alternative for many players.

That isn't even mentioning the numerous controversies over the years, including taking down community mods, releasing half-baked remasters, and creating unnecessary platform disparities. Rockstar, we don't want your terrible launcher or awful customer support—we want you to listen to your community.

The newest update is a perfect example of why so many players are frustrated. Older heists, which were some of the best ways to earn money, were heavily nerfed so the newest heist could become the "highest-paying" activity. claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features expensive in-game item pricing and heavily relies on microtransactions like Shark Cards.

citations.review_text:
GTA 5 is one of the best single-player games, as almost everyone knows. Right now I'm not evaluating its story mode. This review is solely about its online mode. 
Personally, I love grind games, especially achievements that are hard to obtain.  In total, I've probably put in 1,200 hours (600 hours on Steam Legacy, 100 hours on Enhanced, and about 500 hours on Xbox). Despite this, GTA Online is one of the worst games that doesn't care about your free time. The game mechanics are filled with senselessly drawn-out actions: want to take down a picture? 10 seconds of doing nothing on a screen; want to hack something? 15 seconds of waiting for a line to fill on the screen. There are countless examples like this that just drag out time, when they could have either simply cut the wait time or had an action happen in 1-2 seconds. 
The ridiculously inflated inflation is another issue. Over the years, the price of simple items has increased so much that you need to grind for several hours just to afford them. There's no need to talk about the prices of sports cars and businesses. We all know why everything is so expensive. Rockstar is an extremely greedy company; they want to sell as many Shark Cards as possible. 
The last update is so terrible, it made me decide to delete the game. I can't remember an update this bad in any game. Did I mention Rockstar is a cheap bastard? They ruined the old content, nerfed the money-making methods, I've lost count of how many times they've crippled Cayo Perico. Why? So they can milk players before GTA 6 is out. On top of that, the new content isn't good either. The Kortz Center Heist is a copy-paste of the casino heist; the setup missions are identical. You'd think it was made by AI.
Modern GTA Online has become like a mobile game, crammed with microtransactions, pay-to-win and pointlessly dragged activities. Based on Rockstar's recent actions, I'm already scared of what GTA 6 will be like in future.

claims.claim: Public online sessions suffer from cheaters, mod menus, and griefing via vehicles like the Oppressor Mk II.

citations.review_text: TO  MANY MODERS AND CHEATERS DONT PLAY IN  PPL  SERVER IS NOT WORTH FOUND SOME FRIENDS TO PLAY  PRIVE

I actually love the core of this game, but I’m leaving a negative review because if the player base doesn't push back on the current state of PC lobbies, the developers are never going to change how they handle networking and PvP.

The PvE: S-Tier
When you are actually allowed to play the game, the PvE is brilliant. The heist setups, the solo business grinding, the properties—it’s genuinely some of the best sandbox progression in gaming. If you can get into an Invite-Only lobby and just run your empire, it is an incredible experience.

The PvP & Technical State: F-Tier
Public lobbies are an absolute unplayable joke right now.

1. The Oppressor Mk II: It completely removes any actual skill or driving from vehicle combat.

2. Limp, Passive-Aggressive Tactics: People will randomly kill you when you spawn on the beach, then instantly job-warp across the map, hide inside an apartment, or leave the session the second you try to fight back. It is incredibly cowardly behavior.

3. Garbage Matchmaking: The peer-to-peer network is so outdated that the game constantly fails its connection handshakes. You will finish a mission and get consistently dumped into a public lobby completely by yourself because the game’s networking simply breaks.

4. Mod Menus & Crashes: Rockstar finally added BattlEye, but it’s completely failing against the current wave of menus. Script kiddies aren't just using menus to script-kick everyone from the session—they can literally force-crash your desktop client, forcing you to Alt+F4 and completely restart your game.

The Future (GTA 6)
With GTA 6 around the corner, Rockstar’s current direction isn’t inspiring confidence. They’ve already confirmed the sequel will be console-only at launch, physical copies are essentially digital-only (just a download code in a plastic box), it's a single-player only experience right now, and they are already locking in-game content behind a $100 Ultimate Edition paywall.

Buy this game for the solo …

citations.review_text: I came back to GTA:O to play around for a bit and see how things had progressed since my days of playing the game on xbox. Did heists (that were nerfed into the ground) and got all the properties to fully realize just how blitheringly tedious playing Online is. Almost every single part of the player experience was put in to make you waste as much time as possible or just flat stonewall you so you can't do anything. I have a thousand little nitpicks that I would be better off making a video essay to cover. But I will say this, Rockstar is a billion dollar company and enterprise that has racked up billions off of this game, and every dollar they put into working on Online was spent making sure that you do not have fun.

After playing this game for almost 2000 hours across all platforms, (PS3, PS4, PS5, PC Enhanced, and PC Legacy) seeing Rockstar stooping as low as going out of their way to nerf each and every single heist to absolute abysmal dog water to a point where the former best heist in the game (Cayo Perico) which used to give out up to $2M+ solo, to now barely paying $400k for the Tequila has made me realize how much not just this game, but Rockstar as a whole has gone to ♥♥♥♥. Our expectations for you were low, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you went lower than the damn earth's core. And to think this was covered up with giving players a one time bonus per week for doing previous heists to promote players "revisiting older content" is an absolute joke. Probably gonna quit GTA after this since as Pavel once said. "I think this is the strike that broke the camel's hump."

Looking past the horrible amount of cheaters that plague the game and the endless amount of bugs plus the new heist and challenges that make absolutely make no sense to complete. The latest patch made it so you get a reduced amount on old heists if you replay them in the same week but instead you will get a slight bonus for each one you do the first time of each week. Do rockstar want people to actually play this game? Why would they implement such a massive nerf such late into the games lifecycle? This absolutely screws over new players that don't have diverse businesses to get their weekly "bonus" for each heist/heist like activity. Us veterans have no trouble going back to selling MC and Bunker stuff and quiting heist activities but if you're a new player? Better buy a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shark card or two! Rockstar make a million dollars a day from this game and introduce even more nerfs to make more money...

claims.claim: Reviewers report that recent updates added a repeating heist located at an art building and tied new content behind expensive mansions.

citations.review_text:
Holy divebomb right into the gutter, Past few years have been tons of QoL doing more SOLO playability and selling... very nice... then they started added REALLY good features... behind GTA+... very cring but most of these features are something most well off players really don't need....

Final final for real final heist hitting that same damn art building we've flown over a thousand times, in that fancy new mansion with neiche perks as a heist place... insanely overpriced racking up to 18+MILLION. Sure we have mega millions jumbo jets but money dumps are not the problem. The new heist is slapdash, kitbash, rushed, buggy, pays poorly, with NO SPLITTING OF CUTS???? And after the first Per week, you get less than the worst cayo luck and bags.

AND THEN THE PRICE CUTS????? AND THEN THE PRICE REDUCTIONS PER REPLAY???????????

rockstar could not bury this game into the grave right before gta6 any harder honestly.

I was initially really excited for the Kortz Center heist update as we hadn't had a proper heist in years. I expected great things since Rockstar had done such great work on the other heists that this one would be the most refined and enjoyable. I was however a little sceptical on it as it was a heavily stealth based heist and stealth in this game has never been the best but I tried to stay positive.

After playing this update I can confidently say that this might has been the worse update to ever release. I'd say it's even worse than the 'San Andreas Mercenaries' update (The one that removed around 200 cars from the websites)

This update nerfed every single heist pay out and they even tried to hide it under a positive change. Now when you play a heist for the first time in a week you get a bonus pay. However if you want to play that heist again within that week then the pay out is dropped significantly, way lower than the original pay outs before the update

The actual heist of this update is broken, annoying, and even unfair at times. Stealth is bad as guards can get trigged over nothing (had once drove up to the checkpoint for the Alpha Mail approach just for it to go loud for no reason why we were in the loading freeze), the laser room is cool but the parts where you have to jump a laser feels more like a gamble on if you avoid it or not, but the worst part of it all is that there are no stealth checkpoints.

The heist has checkpoints but if you screw up and the heist goes loud then you have to restart the whole heist as if you try to die to respawn at your last checkpoint it will spawn you with the alarm blaring regardless if you made to the checkpoint stealth or not. This is in my opinion the worse part of this heist, every other one you can die and start at a checkpoint in stealth but for some reason they made it so this one you can't. That means you can be at the laser vault, set off the alarm, have to quit the heist, start it again, and then do the long dr…

They nerfed all of the heists, and also made it so you can't assign cuts on the new heist, making it so blatantly obvious that all they want for their players, new and old, is to buy shark cards. The new heist has been probably 90% recycled content gameplaywise. The helicopter escape route on it is completely broken, the flyer gets to the end of his path and crashes the damn thing failing the heist every time. A SCRIPTED FLIGHT PATH FAILS THE HEIST EVERY SINGLE TIME YOU TRY IT AND YOU HAVE NO WAY TO STOP IT. SHAME ON YOU ROCKSTAR. TRULY SHAME ON YOU.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that recent updates reduced payouts for existing heists while significantly increasing the cost of in-game properties and items.

citations.review_text: The Kortz Center heist update was greenlit by lobotomized execs with long COVID and CTE. Who tf wants to play a heist with literally a dozen setup missions, guards that pop out of nowhere and set the alarm off, and the clunkiest forced-animation-laser-dodging mechanic that doesn't belong in a game from 2006, let alone an update for a AAA game in 2026? And to top it off, every heist has had their payouts reduced by 30-40%. This is by far the most disgustingly greedy and incompetent update this game has ever gotten in its entire history. It's so obvious that 75% of the devs were laid off and replaced with AI.

The recent Kortz Center Heist update is probably one of the most hated ones, as it ruined the game economy. 

There has been a major nerf on Heist earnings up to 40% on a game where constant grind is considered to be normal due to expensive apartments, mansions, submarines and businesses that can take over 50.000.000$ to purchase and now a 15% cut on a random Cayo Perico Heist gives me less than 160.000$.

The experience for newcomers is going to be horrible especially for solo players with the amount of grind the game now requires.

It was rough but tolerable before on sessions with friends, now it's a nightmare and probably unplayable for solo players.
